content.text: The save path has two layers: a current project document for chat and other JusPrin state, and versioned native model checkpoints for printable state. I’m checking the boundary behavior now so the diagram shows when each layer is written and what a restore actually changes.

In this checkout, JusPrin saves each project locally under the application data directory at `jusprin/projects/<project-id>/`. The project has two kinds of saved data:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Open project in OrcaSlicer] --> B[JusPrin autosave controller]
    B -->|Chat, drafts, plans, intent, print records| C[current-state.json]
    B -->|Geometry, plates, paint, effective settings| D[Model checkpoint]
    E[Attachments] --> F[attachments/]
    C --> G[Managed project folder]
    D --> H[versions/<version-id>/]
    D --> I[resources/]
    H --> G
    I --> G
    F --> G
    J[HEAD] -->|Identifies current version and retained history| H
    G -->|Explicit Export project 3MF| K[User-chosen .3mf file]
```

The *current document* (`current-state.json`) holds conversations, drafts, tool activity, attachments’ records, intent, plans, annotations, and print history. Those edits are coalesced into a write after about 1.5 seconds of quiet, or within 15 seconds during continuous changes. They do not create a model version. [Document fields](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.cpp:382) · [Save scheduling](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:505)

The *model history* holds printable state: geometry, transforms, paint, plates, and effective settings. Each version has Orca 3MF metadata plus references to object resources. Unchanged objects reuse existing resources; changed objects get new ones. `HEAD` is updated only after the new resources and version are written. [Version writer](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:617) · [Commit sequence](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:726)

Opening an external file imports it into this managed store; autosave does not overwrite the source. A standalone `.3mf` is written only when you explicitly export, and that copy does not carry the local conversations or version history. Ordinary Version history restores the model and settings while keeping the current conversation and print records. The proposed “Restore and resume” behavior for chat is documented but **not implemented yet**. [Storage contract](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/agent-docs/jusprin/autosave-version-history.md:1) · [Restore code](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:971)

:codex-annotation{index="1"} Each **newly saved version folder** contains two files:

```text
jusprin/projects/<project-id>/
├── versions/
│   └── <version-id>/
│       ├── manifest.json    # version details and object-resource references
│       └── metadata.3mf     # Orca project metadata
├── resources/
│   └── <resource-id>.zip    # object geometry, shared across versions
├── current-state.json       # current chat and other JusPrin document data
└── HEAD                     # current version and retained-version list
```

`manifest.json` records the version ID, revision, timestamp, project name, original source path, and an `objects` list. Each object entry includes its object ID, backup ID, expected geometry, path inside the 3MF, and the ID of its ZIP in `resources/`. [Manifest format](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:332)

`metadata.3mf` references those object files; it is **not a complete export by itself**. To restore a version, JusPrin combines that metadata with the referenced ZIP resources into a temporary workspace, then loads it through Orca. Unchanged objects can point to the same ZIP from multiple versions. [Version publication](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:670) · [Restore assembly](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:805)

Older version folders may also have a legacy `state.json`. New versions do not copy the current project document into each folder. [Compatibility handling](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:566) · [Test](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp:890)

content.text:
`metadata.3mf` is a **ZIP archive in Orca’s backup 3MF format**. The name is slightly misleading: it holds the project’s configuration, plate layout, object relationships, and other small project records. The large object meshes are stored separately in the version store’s `resources/` directory. JusPrin creates it by calling Orca’s 3MF exporter with `SaveStrategy::Backup`. [Capture call](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:388) · [Backup flags](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Format/bbs_3mf.hpp:125)

A representative archive looks like this; entries marked “if present” depend on the project:

```text
metadata.3mf  (ZIP)
├── [Content_Types].xml
├── _rels/.rels
├── 3D/
│   ├── 3dmodel.model
│   └── _rels/3dmodel.model.rels       (when there are objects)
└── Metadata/
    ├── project_settings.config
    ├── model_settings.config
    ├── slice_info.config
    ├── filament_sequence.json        (if plate data exists)
    ├── process_settings_N.config     (if project presets are embedded)
    ├── filament_settings_N.config    (if embedded)
    ├── machine_settings_N.config     (if embedded)
    ├── layer_heights_profile.txt     (if used)
    ├── layer_config_ranges.xml       (if used)
    ├── brim_ear_points.txt           (if used)
    ├── cut_information.xml           (if used)
    └── custom_gcode_per_layer.xml    (if used)
```

The important pieces are:

- `Metadata/project_settings.config` is **JSON**, despite the `.config` extension. It contains Orca’s combined effective configuration captured from the active preset bundle, including the values needed to reconstruct the print setup. [Configuration capture](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:15757) · [Archive entry writer](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Format/bbs_3mf.cpp:7721)
- `Metadata/model_settings.config` is **XML** containing object and volume attributes and overrides, plus plate information such as bed type, print sequence, and filament mapping. [Object settings](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Format/bbs_3mf.cpp:7784) · [Plate settings](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Format/bbs_3mf.cpp:7908)
- `3D/3dmodel.model` is **XML describing the scene**: model metadata, object components, instance transforms, and the build list. Its components refer to paths such as `/3D/Objects/<name>_<backup-id>.model`; `3D/_rels/3dmodel.model.rels` records those relationships. The referenced mesh files are absent from this ZIP. [Model writer](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Format/bbs_3mf.cpp:6881) · [Relationship writer](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Format/bbs_3mf.cpp:7014)
- `slice_info.config` and the optional files retain plate and specialized project metadata. They are **not sliced G-code**. Backup mode sets `SkipStatic`, which skips embedding G-code, thumbnails, and auxiliary files. [Archive writer](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Format/bbs_3mf.cpp:6377)

On restore, JusPrin reads the version’s `manifest.json`, finds the required shared object ZIPs, and places their geometry beside a copy of `metadata.3mf` in a temporary directory. Orca then loads that assembled backup. This is why `metadata.3mf` alone is not a portable, complete project file. [Restore assembly](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:805)

content.text:
No. A version is intended to reconstruct the **printable model and its saved project settings**. It is not a complete snapshot of every value in the application, and even a successful model restore is not guaranteed to be bit-for-bit identical to the capture.

The concrete differences I found are:

1. **The JusPrin document stays current.** Conversations, drafts, intent, plans, region descriptions, audit entries, and print records live in `current-state.json`, not in each version. Restore explicitly puts the current document back and adds a restore entry. [Restore path](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:971) · [Current-document test](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:8662)

2. **An updated installed preset can change an effective setting.** Orca’s loader can replace settings that were *not customized* in the captured project with values from the currently installed system or inherited preset. For example, if a system preset’s default changes after capture, restoring that version can use the new default. That is a concrete reason my earlier statement that `metadata.3mf` “carries the settings restored with that version” was too absolute. [Preset loading rule](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp:2496)

3. **Loading can normalize or change settings.** Orca applies defaults, normalizes the loaded configuration, and has compatibility conversions for older files. If connected-printer synchronization is enabled, the load path can also select a printer preset matching the connected machine. These paths run when a version is restored because `Restore` includes configuration loading. [Restore flags](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Format/bbs_3mf.hpp:162) · [Normalization](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:6281) · [Printer synchronization](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:6879)

4. **Some data was never checkpointed.** Backup mode omits G-code, thumbnails, and auxiliary files. Print-host connection fields are also removed from the captured effective configuration. The loader selects plate 0 after loading, so even the active plate is not a point-in-time UI restore. [Backup flags](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Format/bbs_3mf.hpp:125) · [Excluded connection fields](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/PresetBundle.cpp:3865) · [Plate selection](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:6945)

There is also an availability limit: retention can remove an unpinned version, and a missing or corrupt resource makes restore fail. The resource check verifies ZIP structure and usable geometry, but it does not compare against a saved content hash, so it is not proof of byte-for-byte identity. [Retention](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:864) · [Resource validation](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:266)

So the accurate contract is **best-effort restoration of a saved printable project through Orca’s current loader**, with current JusPrin document state preserved. It is not an unambiguous replay of every value at capture time.

Not necessarily. The name collision causes the embedded preset to be skipped, but it does **not** by itself discard its saved effective values. The 3MF also contains a combined config, and the loader uses that config when selecting or editing the same-named system preset ([Preset.cpp](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp:1923), [Preset.cpp](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp:2605)).

The risk is in the rebase step we just discussed: values listed in `different_settings_to_system` stay as saved edits; values *not* listed can be replaced from the currently installed inherited or system preset before the edited copy is made ([Preset.cpp](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp:2519), [PrintConfig.cpp](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:10125)).

So I would call the resulting combined config **potentially different from the captured one**, not necessarily wrong whenever names collide. The collision also means the embedded preset itself is not restored as a distinct preset, even if the effective settings happen to match.

content.text:
In current upstream OrcaSlicer, `different_settings_to_system` is a **list of setting names, not their values**. It tells the project loader which values in the saved combined config are overrides that must survive a preset reload.

For an ordinary 3MF project:

1. On save, Orca compares each edited print, filament, and printer preset with its selected parent and records the differing keys. Despite the field’s name, that parent can be an inherited preset, not necessarily a system preset. The array is ordered as `[print, filament 1, …, filament N, printer]` ([save path](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/blob/f3d0b8a553958a10fe94df7d6ca2513d5690e8e3/src/libslic3r/PresetBundle.cpp#L4830-L4844), [serialization](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/blob/f3d0b8a553958a10fe94df7d6ca2513d5690e8e3/src/libslic3r/PresetBundle.cpp#L5070-L5088)).
2. On load, a **listed** key generally keeps its saved value; an **unlisted** key is replaced with the value from the currently available base preset when that base is found. The resulting config is then compared with or applied as an edit to the selected preset ([load path](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/blob/f3d0b8a553958a10fe94df7d6ca2513d5690e8e3/src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp#L1057-L1086), [replacement logic](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/blob/f3d0b8a553958a10fe94df7d6ca2513d5690e8e3/src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp#L11546-L11560)). Per-extruder vector settings have additional merge handling.
3. It also informs warnings about modified custom G-code, and upstream’s CLI now maintains the lists when exporting preset or command-line overrides so reopening the 3MF does not discard them ([validation](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/blob/f3d0b8a553958a10fe94df7d6ca2513d5690e8e3/src/libslic3r/PresetBundle.cpp#L2388-L2457), [CLI](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/blob/f3d0b8a553958a10fe94df7d6ca2513d5690e8e3/src/OrcaSlicer.cpp#L2067-L2111)).

So its central behavior is **override-versus-inheritance on reopen**. For example, if the file says `wall_loops=4`, listing `wall_loops` preserves 4; omitting it allows the current base preset’s value to replace 4. Upstream has an end-to-end test asserting exactly that distinction ([test](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/blob/f3d0b8a553958a10fe94df7d6ca2513d5690e8e3/tests/cli/test_cli_project_missing_keys.sh#L1-L9)).

Yes—assuming `wall_loops` is the key you mean and Orca finds that base print preset, the in-memory value becomes **2**. The loader treats an unlisted key as inherited and replaces the saved `3` with the current base value ([load logic](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/blob/f3d0b8a553958a10fe94df7d6ca2513d5690e8e3/src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp#L11546-L11560)). Upstream even tests that behavior ([test](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/blob/f3d0b8a553958a10fe94df7d6ca2513d5690e8e3/tests/cli/test_cli_project_missing_keys.sh#L1-L9)).

Whether it’s a bug depends on *when* the preset was 2:

- If it was **3 at capture** and changed to **2 later**, the omission is expected: Orca intentionally follows the new inherited value.
- If it was **already 2 at capture** while the project saved **3**, `wall_loops` should have been listed. Its omission is a save/metadata inconsistency, and loading silently loses the saved value.

Either way, it means `project_settings.config` alone is **not an exact-replay snapshot** of effective settings.

If we **stipulate** that the field omits `wall_loops` despite A’s parent having 2, then yes: with that parent available, loading can replace the saved 3 with 2—even though B’s same-named preset has 3. But that omission would be inconsistent with the normal save path. I haven’t established that Orca produces such an omission in your scenario.

content.text:
Yes. The coherent design principle is **“save a preset plus its overrides,” not “freeze every setting at its saved value.”** That’s my reading of the implementation, not a formal upstream design statement. Orca’s documented preset inheritance works the same way: a child inherits settings it hasn’t overridden, so parent updates can flow through ([profile guide](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/wiki/how_to_create_profiles)).

A useful mental model for opening a normal project is:

`restored settings ≈ current base preset + saved keys marked as overrides`

`project_settings.config` contains full values, but `different_settings_to_system` decides which of those values win over the current base. The loader explicitly replaces unlisted values from the base ([loader](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/blob/f3d0b8a553958a10fe94df7d6ca2513d5690e8e3/src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp#L1057-L1086), [replacement](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/blob/f3d0b8a553958a10fe94df7d6ca2513d5690e8e3/src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp#L11546-L11560)).

That explains the intent: **your edits stay; inherited defaults can update.** It also explains why this feels messy: the file *looks* like a complete snapshot, embedded presets *look* self-contained, and same-name presets can collide, but the loader still applies preset-inheritance rules. For exact version-history restoration, that is a poor fit: a saved 3MF is not guaranteed to reproduce every effective value later or on another machine.
